steps.name: Variance partitioning: condition vs sex vs age
caveats: The record does not state whether the Salmon counts are length-corrected; DESeq2 size-factor normalization plus vst absorbs per-gene scale differences, so treat the delivered counts as raw and note the uncertainty in the report.

If the model matrix is rank-deficient (e.g., sex perfectly confounded with condition), report the non-estimable term, drop it, rerun the estimable model, and state exactly which term was dropped and why - never silently.
With n = 12 the per-gene type-II SS are highly variable; treat the pooled overall fractions as the primary estimate and per-gene medians as the distributional summary.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-without-variance-partition-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples + gene-ID column; Salmon gene-level counts; the record does not state whether length correction was applied) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-variance-partition-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, sex F/M, age in years). Single batch. R toolchain available: DESeq2, vegan (varpart), car, ggplot2. Use all 12,000 genes; no filtering in this step.
steps.question: In the 12 human adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired), what fraction of expression variance is explained by treatment condition, sex, and age respectively, and how do the three factors rank?
constraints: Build the 12,000 x 12 count matrix from counts.csv (row names = gene IDs) and verify all 12 column names match metadata rows exactly; fail loudly on any mismatch.
Variance-stabilize with DESeq2::vstTransform (design ~ sex + age + condition, blind = FALSE) and run all decompositions on the vst values, not raw counts.

Per gene, fit lm(vst ~ condition + sex + age) and compute type-II sum of squares for condition, sex, age (car::Anova(type = 2)) plus SStot and SSres; per-gene fraction for each factor = SS_factor / SStot.

Aggregate two ways and report both: (a) overall pooled fraction per factor = sum of SS_factor over all genes / sum of (SS_condition + SS_sex + SS_age + SSres) over all genes; (b) median and IQR of the per-gene fractions per factor.
Run varpart::varpart on the vst matrix with the three factors as well, and report its adjusted R-squared and the standard Venn fractions as a cross-check.

Report covariate balance: sex counts within each condition group, age min/median/max per condition group, and correlation of each covariate with condition; state explicitly whether condition is confounded or imbalanced with sex or age.
State the power limitation plainly: 12 samples, 3 non-intercept parameters (8 residual df), so per-gene fractions are noisy and the pooled estimates carry wide uncertainty.

Produce: a table (factor -> overall fraction, median per-gene fraction, IQR per-gene fraction) that sums with the residual to 1; a varpart Venn plot; a distribution plot (violin/box) of per-gene condition fractions; a one-paragraph ranking of condition vs sex vs age.
steps.description: Per-gene and pooled decomposition of expression variance into condition, sex, and age components on DESeq2 vst-transformed values, with covariate-balance diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Variance table with fractions for condition, sex, age (pooled overall + per-gene median/IQR) that sum with the residual to 1.
varpart decomposition with adjusted R-squared and a Venn figure.
Covariate-balance table (sex per condition, age range per condition) and an explicit 8-residual-df caveat in the write-up.

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: If DESeq2 reports a non-estimable coefficient (sex or age confounded with condition), report the confounding, rerun with the reduced design, and state which term was dropped and why.
6 vs 6, single batch, three covariates consuming 3 of 8 residual df: expect few significant genes. Do not relax the FDR threshold to manufacture significance; report what the FDR actually returns.
steps.context: Same inputs as T1S1: counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level counts as delivered) and metadata.csv (condition, sex, age). R toolchain: DESeq2, apeglm, ggplot2. This step is the answer to the second half of the research question and feeds the enrichment step.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control in human adipose after adjusting for sex and age?
constraints: Fit DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age + condition, condition coded as a two-level factor (treated vs control) and placed last so the default contrast is treated vs control.
Keep all 12,000 genes in the fit; report how many were retained after independentFiltering.
Shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm (lfcShrink(..., type = 'apeglm')).

Output the full results table for all genes: gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunk LFC, pvalue, padj; plus the significant lists at padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1; plus a volcano plot and an MA plot.

Power reporting: histogram of p-values, the observed p < 0.05 rate against the 5% null expectation, and the minimum |LFC| that reaches padj < 0.05 at a baseMean of ~500, so the effect-size detection limit of 6 vs 6 samples is explicit.
Record in the report that the delivered Salmon gene-level counts are treated as raw and that the record does not state whether length correction was applied.
steps.description: DESeq2 full design ~ sex + age + condition with apeglm-shrunk log2FC, producing the treated-vs-control DE table, significance lists, plots, and a power assessment.
acceptance_criteria: DE table covering all 12,000 genes with shrunken LFC and padj, and significance lists at padj < 0.05 and padj < 0.1.

A power statement tied to the observed p-value distribution and observed dispersion, not generic boilerplate; if padj < 0.05 is empty, the count is reported as 0 with top nominal hits (p < 0.01) listed separately and clearly labeled uncorrected.

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes and ranked list
caveats: With 7,538 GO BP sets the FDR burden is heavy: report nominal and q-value significance both and do not over-read a single GO hit.
If T1S2 found no padj < 0.05 genes, run GSEA on the ranked list as the sole primary result and say so; do not force an ORA on an empty list.
Hallmark hits are coarse 50-set summaries; pair any Hallmark hit with the specific GO/ WikiPathways sets behind it before interpreting mechanism.
steps.context: Input: the T1S2 DE table (gene, baseMean, log2FC, shrunk LFC, pvalue, padj) and the T1S2 ranked list. Human gene sets staged in this environment include MSigDB Hallmark human (50 sets), MSigDB human GO (BP/CC/MF), WikiPathways human, and MSigDB human canonical pathways - resolve them by content from the environment, not by hardcoded paths. All sets use HGNC symbols, so gene IDs must be mapped to symbols first.
steps.question: Which human biological processes and pathways are enriched among the treated-vs-control DE genes and in the full ranked list?
constraints: Convert DE-table gene IDs to HGNC symbols first (the counts.csv ID space is not confirmed to be symbols - it may be Ensembl or Entrez; map via org.Hs.eg.db or the staged UniProt human ID-mapping table), report the mapping rate for the significant list and the ranked list, and stop with a clear report if < 80% of significant genes map.

ORA on the padj < 0.05 DE list against MSigDB Hallmark human and human GO BP (clusterProfiler::enricher or equivalent). If the DE list has fewer than 20 genes, run ORA on the top 100 genes by padj, label it as a fallback, and make GSEA the primary result.
GSEA: rank all 12,000 genes by sign(shrunk LFC) * -log10(pvalue) and run fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark human and human GO BP; report the top 20 sets per collection with NES and FDR q.
Run WikiPathways human as a secondary collection for both ORA and GSEA and report it separately.
For GO BP, report redundancy explicitly (nested hierarchy) - give the count of significant sets and, where practical, collapse to the most specific significant sets.
Output: ORA table, GSEA table (top 20 per collection), dot/bar plots of top pathways, and a 3-5 sentence interpretation of which processes the treatment perturbed in adipose, tied to DE direction.
steps.description: Over-representation analysis on the DE list and fgsea GSEA on the full ranked list against human reference gene sets, with symbol-mapping audit and a short interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: ORA and GSEA tables with q-values against at least MSigDB Hallmark human and human GO BP.
Symbol-mapping rate reported for both the DE list and the ranked list.
Top-pathway figure(s) and a short interpretation consistent with the DE direction.

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partitioning and DE
plan.analytical_narrative: Human adipose bulk RNA-seq: 12 samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch), Salmon gene-level counts 12,000 genes x 12 samples, with condition, sex (F/M), and age (years) per sample in metadata.csv. The question is answered in the order asked: first partition per-gene expression variance into condition vs sex vs age (per-gene type-II ANOVA on DESeq2 vst values plus a pooled varpart decomposition) — this quantifies how separable the treatment signal is from the covariates and sets power expectations for the contrast; then run DESeq2 with the full design ~ sex + age + condition so the treated-vs-control test is adjusted for both covariates, with apeglm-shrunk LFCs; finally map the DE list and the full ranked list to the human gene sets staged in the environment (MSigDB Hallmark human, human GO, WikiPathways human) to interpret which genes changed. Single batch, so no batch-correction step. The 12,000 x 12 matrix is small; every step runs on modest resources.
